world.setting: Contemporary offices, meeting rooms, living rooms and kitchens — Stuart's firm, Marita's sofa, a boardroom
world.register: workplace-psychology explainer — everyday offices and phone calls, not history or fantasy

stuart.name: Stuart
stuart.role: case subject — entrepreneur in his 60s, the feared Red boss with the red/green office lamp
stuart.look: White man in his sixties, heavy build, receding gray hair, dark suit, stern impatient face

marita.name: Marita
marita.role: Erikson's sister — the embodiment of pure Yellow, cross-legged on the sofa telling stories
marita.look: White woman in her late thirties, medium build, long loose blonde hair, bright patterned blouse, laughing mid-gesture

bjorn.name: Bjorn
bjorn.role: staged example caller — the classic Red on the phone, asks about a sick daughter then hangs up
bjorn.look: White man in his early forties, short-cropped dark hair, clean-shaven square jaw, navy blazer over white shirt

erikson.name: Thomas Erikson
erikson.role: author/host — the explainer of the four-color system
erikson.look: White man in his late fifties, average build, short graying hair, glasses, plain blazer over shirt

green.name: Green (the stable colleague)
green.role: the Green type — steady, warm and conflict-avoidant; says yes, then quietly refuses to row
green.look: White man in his fifties, sturdy build, plain green vest over a pale shirt, short brown hair, calm patient face

blue.name: Blue (the precise analyst)
blue.role: the Blue type — analytical, prepared, quality-obsessed; needs the facts and the time to check them
blue.look: White woman in her forties, slight build, blue coat over a pale blouse, dark hair in a bun, thin glasses, measured precise face

everyman.name: Everyman
everyman.role: viewer stand-in — the colleague, partner, or manager learning to translate
everyman.look: Neutral adult office worker, medium build, plain casual shirt, no striking features

office.look: Modern open-plan office with desks, a meeting table, and one feared corner office with a lamp above the door

room.look: Ordinary living room with a sofa — Marita cross-legged mid-story

kitchen.look: Ordinary home kitchen table with one chair sat in every morning for five years

cafe.look: Small sidewalk cafe table with an espresso cup, town square beyond

objects.why: Every clash staged as call or email thread — Bjorn's call about the sick daughter, blunt texts vs exclamation-mark novels
The office is the laboratory — Stuart's firm, the red-CEO meeting, junior consultants, software debate
Reds aim at results and velocity; the four-color grid itself is a targeting diagram
Color collisions as win/lose encounters — boardroom standoffs, who adapts and who steamrolls
Blue precision vs Yellow chaos — sticky notes, paper piles, bullet essays, spreadsheets on time
Office hospitality rituals — brewing coffee for clients while drowning in workload (Green self-sacrifice)
Stress masks slip — Reds explode, Yellows joke-deflect, Greens withdraw, Blues turn cold
False-consensus mirror — everyone assumes their own brain is the objective default
Time is the Red currency — velocity, slammed tables, lingering pleasantries as waste
Stuart's office door with the red/green lamp — the company reads one door before approaching

signatureObjects.name: Four-Color Grid
signatureObjects.why: The book's central artifact — two axes making Red/Yellow/Green/Blue quadrants. No shared icon depicts a 2x2 behavior matrix; the film returns to it every beat.

signatureObjects.name: Stuart's Red/Green Office Lamp
signatureObjects.why: The red/green lamp above Stuart's office door the whole company checks before approaching — the most concrete image of Red terror ruling a workplace. No shared icon depicts a door signal lamp.

spine.claim: You are not surrounded by idiots — you assume your own brain is the default while everyone else thinks YOU are the idiot.
The four colors decoded — Red speed, Yellow energy, Green stability, Blue precision — each strength is another color's flaw.
Under stress the mask slips — the Red CEO slams the table, the Green withdraws, the Yellow deflects, the Blue freezes.
Reading people takes two minutes — pace, voice, posture, email style — and observation beats stereotyping.
Adaptation is translation not faking — same message in four colors, and the idiots disappear.
